title: Privacy, Security and Compliance
summary: LLM features move user text through many systems: prompts, logs, caches, vector stores and third-party providers. This lesson treats privacy and security as engineering: data flows and classification, retention, minimisation, tenant isolation, secrets and the audit trail that compliance depends on. It states principles, not legal advice.
objectives: Map the data flow of an LLM feature and classify what each store holds
Quantify exposure from retention periods and cut it with a retention policy
Explain why combinations of harmless fields can identify a person, and apply data minimisation
Design tenant isolation for retrieval, caches and logs, and see why filtering must happen before ranking
Handle secrets and API keys with least privilege, rotation and spend caps
Describe the engineering evidence that audits and data-subject requests rely on
prerequisites: You should know how a RAG pipeline stores documents in a vector index ([How RAG Works](/learn/retrieval-and-rag/rag-architecture)), what PII redaction is ([Guardrails and Safe Deployment](/learn/production-systems/guardrails)) and what a request log contains ([Observability and Incident Analysis](/learn/production-systems/observability)). This lesson gives engineering principles only. It is not legal advice: laws differ by country and industry, so involve your legal and security teams for decisions.
